metadata.title: Bug bounty program profile
metadata.description: Capture source-backed program authority, exact scope, technique permissions, execution bounds, evidence handling, hypothesis-led depth, coverage, reporting expectations, and separately bound recommendations before an engagement is materialized. Imported material is evidence only and never executes, grants authority, or changes policy.

sections.title: Identity, objectives, and completion
sections.purpose: Define the program, the testing outcome, and what a satisfactory finished assessment must contain.

questions.prompt: What is the exact program or engagement name?
questions.why: The name anchors private records and generated reports to the correct program.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only a validated observed or inferred source/local proposal; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: What concrete security outcome should this assessment achieve?
questions.why: A precise objective keeps exploration useful and gives the final report an assessable purpose.

recommendationPolicy.value: Produce a source-backed, end-to-end security assessment that follows promising signals through reproducible validation and reports every tested, blocked, and unresolved branch.
recommendationPolicy.summary: Use GATE’s end-to-end, evidence-backed assessment objective.
recommendationPolicy.basis: Operator preferences OP-SEC-001, OP-SEC-003, and OP-SEC-004.

questions.prompt: How deep should the assessment go, including how far promising signals must be followed?
questions.why: Targeted means deep work on a narrow objective, thorough adds prioritized signal follow-up to the baseline map, and exhaustive requires a disposition for relevant hypotheses and high-friction tests. Surface checks alone do not satisfy thorough or exhaustive depth.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use thorough depth with prioritized follow-up beyond baseline mapping.

questions.prompt: Which deliverables must be produced?
questions.why: Explicit deliverables prevent an otherwise useful assessment from missing the form the operator or program expects.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use the standard technical report, evidence, coverage, retest, and cleanup set.
recommendationPolicy.basis: Operator preferences OP-KNO-001, OP-KNO-004, and OP-SEC-001.

questions.prompt: What observable conditions make this assessment satisfactory, including how promising signals and blocked or untested high-friction work must be dispositioned?
questions.why: Success criteria distinguish completion from merely running tools or collecting output and keep unresolved hypotheses visible instead of silently ending at surface coverage.

value: Every selected coverage domain has a recorded disposition.
Every promising signal has an evidence-backed conclusion or a visible blocker.
Every applicable high-friction scenario is tested, not applicable, blocked, or explicitly untested.
Target-side changes have a recorded cleanup and verification outcome.
recommendationPolicy.summary: Require dispositions for coverage, promising signals, high-friction tests, and cleanup.
recommendationPolicy.basis: Operator preferences OP-SEC-003, OP-SEC-004, and OP-KNO-001.

sections.title: Authority and source ledger
sections.purpose: Record the sources that establish authority and program terms, their freshness, and the contacts who can clarify or stop work.

questions.prompt: List every rules, scope, safe-harbor, contract, architecture, account, and operator source used by this profile.
questions.why: Every decisive claim cites this ledger so changed or unsupported terms can be detected instead of inferred.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: What is the exact basis for authorization?

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: What canonical program URL applies, or null when no program URL exists?
questions.why: A canonical location makes rules revalidation deterministic without treating retrieved text as executable instructions.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Only the operator can confirm that reviewed sources authorize the described work.

sections.title: Actions and techniques
sections.purpose: Classify every GATE action and each program-specific technique without treating silence as permission.

questions.prompt: Which assistance modes should GATE provide for this program?
questions.why: Explicit plan, analyze, command-generation, execution, reporting, and retest intent lets compilation choose compatible model and tool capabilities without silently expanding the request.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Enable every GATE assistance mode while leaving execution authority unchanged.
recommendationPolicy.basis: Operator preferences OP-WRK-001, OP-WRK-002, and OP-SEC-001.

questions.prompt: For each of the 13 action labels, is it allowed, denied, conditional, or unknown?
questions.why: Every action needs its own source-backed decision; conditional and unknown answers never compile as allowed.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: Which named techniques need more specific rules than their action label, especially stateful, multi-step, concurrent, timing-sensitive, callback or webhook, role or tenant matrix, and differential tests?
questions.why: Program terms often distinguish high-friction automation, credential testing, callbacks, persistence, or data access within the same broad action. Naming these techniques makes tests that are costly or error-prone to perform manually available for exact planning.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: Which IANA timezone governs all testing windows?

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use an observed local IANA timezone or a source-derived proposal; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: On which days and times may work occur?

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum duration for one execution?
questions.why: A wall-clock ceiling bounds stalled or unexpectedly slow work.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum request count for one execution?
questions.why: A request ceiling turns an open-ended operation into a bounded test plan.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum concurrency?
questions.why: Concurrency affects target load even when the average rate appears acceptable.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum request or packet rate per second?
questions.why: A rate ceiling captures short bursts that a total request limit cannot.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum model-token budget for one run?
questions.why: A token ceiling makes model cost and context use visible and comparable.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Start with a visible 50,000-token budget per run.
recommendationPolicy.basis: Operator preference to make token use visible and bounded.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum external spend in USD? Use 0 to prohibit spending; null explicitly means no monetary ceiling was supplied.
questions.why: Zero is an explicit prohibition. Null records that no monetary ceiling was supplied and must never be interpreted as a prohibition.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Prohibit external spend until the operator sets a different ceiling.

questions.prompt: Which source IDs establish these limits?
questions.why: Limit values must remain traceable when program rules or operator decisions change.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: List every typed asset selector with its disposition, provenance, rationale, conditions, complete per-action decisions, and exact execution-limit envelope.
questions.why: Each asset must carry its own effective action and limit policy so a broad global rule cannot silently authorize a narrower or adjacent target. Global action and limit rules remain ceilings.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: How must third-party services, shared infrastructure, and vendors be handled?

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: May tools follow redirects, aliases, or alternate authorities, and under what conditions?
questions.why: Redirects and aliases can cross the exact selector boundary even when the starting URL is allowed.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: What happens when reconnaissance discovers an asset absent from the cited scope?

questions.prompt: Define each execution slice with a unique ID, workflow phase ID, exact asset refs and actions, allowed and denied tool IDs, conditions, claim state, source refs, tighter limit overrides, and any deeper automated branch it is meant to support.
questions.why: Phase slices keep tool use, target contact, provenance, resource ceilings, and high-friction follow-up bound to exact assets and workflow phases instead of flattening global rules across the program.

sections.title: Data and evidence handling
sections.purpose: Define what data may be observed, where evidence may go, how long it is retained, and what constitutes sufficient proof.

questions.prompt: What is the highest data classification expected in evidence?
questions.why: Classification drives model routing, storage, redaction, and reporting decisions.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Treat expected evidence as restricted until source-backed handling supports a lower classification.

questions.prompt: Which evidence destinations are explicitly permitted?
questions.why: Collected material must not leave the destinations approved by the program and operator.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Keep evidence in the private local GATE home by default.
recommendationPolicy.basis: Operator preference OP-PUR-003 and GATE private-state policy.

questions.prompt: How many days may private evidence be retained?
questions.why: A retention period makes cleanup and closeout verifiable.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: Which data must be redacted, minimized, or never captured?
questions.why: Specific redaction rules reduce unnecessary exposure while preserving reproducible proof.

value: Remove credentials, authentication artifacts, unrelated personal data, and unnecessary record content.
recommendationPolicy.summary: Use the standard credential and data-minimization rule.
recommendationPolicy.basis: GATE’s symbolic-secret and minimum-proof handling policy.

questions.prompt: What is the least evidence needed to validate impact?
questions.why: A minimum-proof rule limits unnecessary record access or extraction after impact is established.

recommendationPolicy.value: Stop collecting or accessing data once the smallest reproducible evidence set establishes the security impact.
recommendationPolicy.summary: Collect only the smallest reproducible proof needed to establish impact.

questions.prompt: Which symbolic env, keychain, or file references may be resolved at execution time?
questions.why: Only references belong in the profile; credential values stay outside repository and general logs.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only a validated observed or inferred source/local proposal; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: Which source IDs establish the evidence-handling rules?
questions.why: Destinations and retention are receipt-relevant terms and must be traceable.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

sections.title: Stops, escalation, and cleanup
sections.purpose: Define the response for all 13 mandatory stops, the emergency contacts, and how target-side state is restored and verified.

questions.prompt: What response is required for each of the 13 mandatory stop conditions?
questions.why: Every mandatory stop remains enabled; response detail makes stopping, evidence preservation, and safe teardown repeatable.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: Who receives urgent scope, stability, data, defensive-control, or cleanup escalations?
questions.why: A reachable escalation path prevents an uncertain event from becoming an improvised decision.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: Must every target-side change be cleaned up or explicitly held for recovery?
questions.why: The workflow requires deterministic cleanup accounting for any stateful test.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Require cleanup or an explicit recovery hold for every target-side change.

questions.prompt: Which cleanup steps apply to accounts, files, records, sessions, callbacks, infrastructure, or other test state?
questions.why: Predefined steps allow safe teardown after an ordinary completion, stop, or authorization expiry.

value: Remove test data and callbacks, revoke temporary sessions and credentials, and account for every retained target-side change.
recommendationPolicy.summary: Use the standard target-state cleanup checklist as the starting point.

questions.prompt: How will restoration be verified?
questions.why: A cleanup action is incomplete until evidence shows the intended state was restored.

recommendationPolicy.value: Verify the restored state with the smallest non-destructive check and preserve a private evidence reference.
recommendationPolicy.summary: Verify restored state with a minimal non-destructive check.

questions.prompt: Which source IDs establish cleanup requirements?
questions.why: Cleanup obligations need the same provenance as authorization and scope.

recommendationPolicy.summary: Use only an observed, source-derived proposal with cited current sources; otherwise leave this question unresolved.

questions.prompt: Which report sections and evidence elements are mandatory?
